text:
maria: FYI we're seeing a steady host-side CPU rise on short-chat traffic after the recent transport changes. p95 drifted ~14% over baseline. digging in now.
cheng: rough symptom list? syscall vs CPU in our libs?
maria: perf top shows clustering in writev, grpc frame assembly, and the tokenizer hotpath. snippet:
```
 samples  %  cmd    so                 symbol
 4200    31% hostd  libc.so.6          __writev
 1300     9% hostd  grpc_core.so       grpc_call_start_batch
 1100     8% hostd  host_tokenizer.so  tokenize_batch
 800      6% hostd  host_kv.so         kv_lookup
```
maria: surprisingly kv_lookup spiked too (hotset churn).
alex: Suspect two things: (1) transport now emits lots of tiny iovecs after http2 header rewrite, and (2) our preparse/pretokenize flow creates different cache keys when enabled -> evict pressure.
sam: Also the kernel selector is picking a throughput-favoring kernel for small single-request batches because our heuristic is based on average seq_len across queue, and short bursts get misclassified.
tao: can we short-circuit selector for packets < 48 tokens? use a low-latency fp16 path.
cheng: Proposed quick fixes:
- implement a transport-level writev coalescer for iovecs < 2kb (coalesce adjacent small iovs)
- add ingress flag `preparse_skip_threshold` to skip preparse for very short sequences
- kernel selector override: if candidate_batch == 1 and seq_len < N then prefer low-latency kernel
- normalize KV cache keys when preparse is off (stable hashing)
alex: I'll prototype the writev coalescer (should be confined to grpc transport shim). cheap wins.
maria: tao/maria will work the selector override. raj is out but can pick up KV key normalization. sam you ok to run perf buckets?
sam: yes. quick local microbench (short-chat dataset, 10k qps):
```
baseline: host_cpu 100%, p50 22ms, p95 180ms
w/ coalescer: host_cpu 92%, p50 23ms, p95 150ms
w/ coalescer + preparse-skip: host_cpu 86%, p50 24ms, p95 120ms
```
sam: notable: cpu down ~14% combined, p95 improved 33%. p50 slightly up because we skipped preparse (one extra tokenize on hotpath) but accept tradeoff.
cheng: Good. Do we have safety telemetry? add metrics: `ingress.preparse_skipped_total`, `transport.writev_coalesced_total`, `selector.forced_lowlat`.
infra-bot: Canary kick: rolling to canary-hosts-3 at 1762140000. routing 8k short-rps for 45m.
infra-bot: Canary summary (45m):
- host_cpu: -13.2%
- p50_lat: +0.6ms
- p95_lat: -28%
- kv_evictions/min: -30%
- transport.writev_coalesced_total: 18.3k
- ingress.preparse_skipped_total: 14.1k

maria: Nice. We should land as a small coordinated patchset: transport coalesce (safe), preparse skip gated by seq_len, selector override, kv key normalization. Roll to Dedicated canaries first then Hosted.
tao: note: add unit test for coalescer to ensure we don't exceed max iov size on the wire. also watch for head-of-line increases in HTTP2 stream ordering.
alex: will include a toggle `transport.coalesce_enabled` default true in canary.
sam: I'll update dashboards and add an alert if `transport.writev_coalesced_total` drops unexpectedly (regression). also add a perf job to run nightly with short-chat trace.
cheng: Is there any reason not to ship this in the next patch? looks low risk.
maria: risk: large-request median could regress slightly if we mis-skip preparse; but our skip is gated by seq_len and only affects requests < 48 tokens. we'll monitor.
raj: :thumbsup: when PRs are up pls link them here.
maria: PRs opened: host/transport coalesce (#4123), ingress preparse skip (#4124), selector override (#4125), kv-normalize (#4126). tagging @eng-sre for rollout.
cheng: thanks everyone. followups: perf diffs, canary 24h run in eu-west, dashboards updated, and add changelog entry for host-runtime patch.
tao: ok to close once 24h canary is green.
alex: 👍
